title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential: The student must state the correct electric field magnitude of 100 N/C, derived from the force balance qE = mg.

title: Electric field direction
description: Essential: The student must correctly identify the electric field direction as vertically upward to balance gravity for a positive charge.

title: Velocity magnitude
description: Essential: The student must calculate the correct incident velocity of 1.5 m/s, using the Lorentz force as centripetal force with the correct radius.

title: Maximum time calculation
description: Essential: The student must provide the correct maximum time of 4.2 s (or equivalent with 2 significant figures).

title: Radius from geometry
description: Important: The student must correctly determine the circular motion radius (r = 1.5 m) using the geometry of the equilateral triangle.

title: Force balance reasoning
description: Important: The student must explain that the electric force balances gravity to enable uniform circular motion in the magnetic field.

title: Maximum angle identification
description: Important: The student must identify that the maximum central angle for the trajectory is 4π/3 radians (or 240°) based on the geometry of point D exit.

title: Time-angle relationship
description: Important: The student must correctly relate the motion time to the central angle using t = (θ/2π)T or t = θm/(qB).

title: Significant figures
description: Optional: The student should present the final time with exactly 2 significant figures as requested.

title: Incorrect force balance
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly balances forces (e.g., omitting gravity or electric field) or uses wrong signs.

title: Wrong geometric radius
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses an incorrect radius (e.g., L instead of PD) for the circular motion calculation.

title: Angle or period error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses the wrong central angle (e.g., 120° instead of 240°) or incorrect period formula.
